  Regular Meeting Minutes
  August 14, 2025

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Vice Chair Ruiz

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Executive Assistant
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, Secretary Cynthia Esquivel and Commissioner Edgar Pelayo.
Staff: Deputy Director Tina Fierro, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, Salomon Lopez, Recreation
Coordinator, and Franklyn Arroyo, Fitness Coordinator.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES
Regular Meeting Minutes of April 10, 2025 and May 8, 2025
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Pelayo

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Fitness Coordinator Franklin Arroyo, he explained the new fitness classes being offered, step
aerobics, yoga, combo boxing class, and a HIIT class. Invited the Commissioners

Recognized: Daniel Canal, volunteers with the SGJAA, whose board is all volunteers, providing low cost
team play to the community. As a partner organization, they are offered fields and courts as the City
provides to the other partner organizations, like AYSO, Aztecs Youth Football, and the Aquatics Team the
uses the pool for free. Wanted to point out to the commission how great the JAA is for the community.

Recognized: Edith Lilly, asked for help in getting a refund from the SGJAA. She’s sent emails, but hasn’t
gotten a response.

Recognized: Roberto Sanchez, requests more pickle ball courts in the parks. It’s a great sport for seniors, it
has become a popular sport.

Recognized: Ernest Medina, a board member for the JAA organization, there was a board of review on Ms.
Edith, her kids weren’t kicked out, the team is still actively playing, she voluntarily took them out, they
were not asked to leave. They were offered credit since refunds are not given. The coach left the team,
it’s a Peanut division, score is not kept, the children are there to learn the fundamentals to prepare them
for the next level.

Deputy Dir. De La Rosa read emails that were submitted for Public Comment:
Candice Solache wants to address Council Member Avalos’ question at the conclusion of the August 12
council meeting, asking if the JAA has insurance and if guidelines exist between the City and the JAA. This
stems from an individual that is not happy that the four- and five-year-olds don’t play competitive games.
Her opinion is Council Member Avalos’ complaint is political to discredit Mayor Barron; this has happened
in the past. Urges the Commission to rise above petty politics and focus on serving our community with
integrity and respect. And avoid divisive and unproductive attacks.

  Page 1 of 4
  4
 Alma Ochoa volunteers for the SGJAA, feels that the attacks of the JAA are politically motivated. Council
Member Avalos referred to a parent’s request for $80. The parent signed a contract that states no refunds
will be issued. The issue began because the coach was not following the rules, and he’s the husband of the
complainant, and was playing competitively regardless of their age and he decided to leave the team.
Council Member Avalos did not reach out to the JAA board instead she politicized the situation.

Evelyn Andrade has been part of the parks and recreation programs for three years. When my children
played against the purple team they were treated very aggressively by the coach. One of our players was
crying. I feel the coach failed his commitment to the team. Please consider all sides and thank you.

Mary Sanchez as a parent of a child in JAA, I and very concerned with the comments made my Council
Member Avalos at the conclusion of the August 12, 2025 Council meeting. She questioned the integrity of
the JAA, based on a single parent complaint. The JAA has always been respectful of the players and
parents. The coach left the team and within 24 hours a replacement had been found; the coach and his
wife still attend JAA games of their older child. How many other Council Members or Commissioners
volunteer in youth programs? What I have seen during Council meetings and social media these attacks
seem to be politically motivated. Respectfully, stop using this youth program for political attacks.

Cynthia Cypert Durning the JAA board meeting Ms. Lilly came in with two other parents and stated that
was upset that this division was not competitive, that is what she signed up for as did her husband, the
coach, and it was explained to him in the coaching contract. One of the parents said he wanted his child to
keep playing. The contract Ms. Lilly signed clearly states No Refunds. After the coach quit in eight hours
we had another coach, so the children can still play and practice without disruption. She asked for a copy
of the minutes, I tried to explain to her that Park staff doesn’t have access to our minutes and we do not
fall under the Sunshine Laws and are not government affiliated so our minutes are not open to the public.
It was hard for others to speak since Ms. Lilly kept interrupting.

Cesar Ochoa want to address a troubling incident during a recent game my child was in. As outlined in the
rules the primary goal for children at this level is to learn the fundamentals. I was very concerned by the
actions of the coach specifically instructing children to aggressively smack and take the ball away from their
peers. This behavior is not appropriate but caused one of the children to cry feeling overwhelmed by the
aggression. I respectfully ask that you review this incident and take appropriate steps to ensure all coaches
foster a positive, supportive environment that encourages participation, skill development and mutual
respect among the children

Jose Luis Mercado I want to express my appreciation to the JAA for its outstanding contributions to the
community. They have made a positive impact for my children; I enrolled seven of my children, who are
now adults; this helped them with their careers in sports. Six of my children are athletic trainers for a
variety of professional worldwide sports. I want to thank the JAA for being an invaluable part of the
community and their continued positive impact.

1. REVIEW OF RECREATION PROGRAMS - 4TH QUARTER 2024/25

M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Esquivel

events. Vice Chair Ruiz said they are great events and thanked the partner organizations for their work.

that since it was brought up a Council it has to stay at that level. She asked how pool staff are affected by

Commissioner Pelayo asked if the switch over of the credit card happened before, Deputy Dir. De La Rosa

2. REVIEW OF GROUNDS & FACILITY MAINTENANCE - 4TH QUARTER 2024/25

Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked if trees that are cut
down are replaced. Parks Supt. Massey explained the replacement procedure. Commissioner Pelayo
asked about the gopher abatement, Parks Supt. Massey stated that different staff has different methods
and the count varies.

3. UPDATE ON PARKS & RECREATION DEPARTMENT MAJOR PROJECTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Secretary Esquivel
Deputy Dir. De La Rosa reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked about the
Auditorium roof project and if the AC would be replaced at the same time; Deputy Dir. De La Rosa said that
the project is in the planning stages and yes the AC will be done at the same time. She also asked about
the huts and the treatment plant storage of chemicals and waste. Deputy Dir. De La Rosa said that they just
had the first meeting. Asked about the Circle Park delays, she was informed of the progress.
Commissioner Pelayo asked if the waste station will require taking down huts; only two, but they will be
replaced. And where did they find additional funding for the Auditorium AC; Deputy Dir. De La Rosa
replied she didn’t know. Chair Flores asked why the low priority for the huts; Parks Supt. Massey explained

4. REPORT FOR ACTIVITIES FOR HALLOWEEN
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo
Recreation Coordinator Salomon Lopez reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Secretary Esquivel
thanked him for the energetic report. Vice Chair Ruiz looks forward to the event. Commissioner Pelayo
hopes to make it as a judge.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Deputy Dir. De La Rosa: Held the Ball’n after Dark event in July, because of its success staff held dodge ball
and volleyball after dark events. We were asked to hold a ball’n after Dark type of event for kids. Staff will
be having one named Bam for high school kids. Concerts in the Park was revamped with food trucks and a
beer garden; they were all well attended. 40 families registered for the Family Camp Out event, had a
great time. Movies in the Park started on Thursday nights at the Golf Course and at Hollydale Community

is holding Museum film screening. The Fun Run was this past Saturday, great event.

Parks Supt. Massey: LA County will holding a free tire recycling event on August 23 at parking lot #6
between 9-3.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Tina De La Rosa, Deputy Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  October 23, 2025
Subject:  Discussion of Street Soccer Presentation

Recommended Motion:  Provide feedback and direction to staff.

Report Summary: To inform the Parks and Recreation Commission of a presentation
by Street Soccer USA, a nonprofit organization, regarding their interest in developing
two Street Soccer fields at Hollydale Regional Park.

Street Soccer USA (SSUSA), a nationally recognized nonprofit, focused on sports-
based youth development, has expressed interest in establishing a presence in South
Gate by building two Street Soccer courts at Hollydale Regional Park. Their mission is
to provide accessible soccer opportunities in underserved communities while promoting
community engagement, health, and youth development.

SSUSA would like to present their concept to the Parks and Recreation Commission,
which includes:
  • Construction of two street soccer fields at Hollydale Regional Park
  • A proposed partnership with AYSO, the youth soccer organization that currently
  practices at the park
  • A goal of providing lighted fields to support evening practices and extended play
  hours
  • A timeline aimed at completing the project prior to the 2026 FIFA World Cup
  • Funding provided by VISA, SSUSA’s corporate sponsor and long-time partner

This proposal has the potential to be a mutually beneficial partnership:
  • AYSO would benefit from limited increased access to lit fields, a need they have
  consistently expressed.
  • Street Soccer USA would bring infrastructure, programming, and community
  resources to South Gate at little to no cost to the City.
  • The project aligns with the City’s goals of improving recreational facilities and
  expanding youth programming opportunities.
  • With the 2026 World Cup approaching, this project could serve as a timely
  enhancement to the City’s sports and community offerings.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  October 23, 2025

Subject:  Review of Recreation Programs 1st Quarter FY 2025/26

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Aquatics
The summer season marked a strong start to the fiscal year at the Swim Stadium. We
brought back Moonlight Lagoon, held Monday through Thursday, 9:00pm - 9:45pm.
Once we reopened on Fridays, we reintroduced an extra Family Swim hour in the
evening 7:30pm - 9:00pm. Family Swim attendance regularly reached capacity,
averaging between 200 - 250 participants per session. Weekend private rentals, were
once again fully booked, maintaining their popularity throughout the whole summer.

We continued to offer a full range of group, private, and semi-private swim lessons for
all ages. This quarter, approximately 1,500 individuals were taught essential swim skills
and water safety. Of those, the majority were for youth (ages 6-17) group lessons, but
we saw steady participation from our Tiny Tots (ages 3-5) and Adults (ages 18+), with
an increase in our Parent & Child (ages 6 mos-2 years) participation. Our private and
semi-private lessons remained strong, with the program being at full capacity all
summer.

Specialty programs also returned in full swing. Gators Swim Academy and Junior
Lifeguard programs, catered to more advanced youth looking for a physical challenge
and leadership development. The program culminated in an end-of-season beach trip
which we combined with our Surfing classes. Feeder programs such as Pre-Competitive
Swim Class and Junior Water Polo saw over 50 registrations combined. We were also
proud to bring back our Summer Splash Camp, a dynamic and fun-filled program
focused on water safety and aquatics sports like diving, water polo, and surfing. The
camp also offered activities such as water balloon tosses, pool volleyball, and aquatic
obstacle courses. Over 150 campers participated over the 8-week season.

  Page 1 of 7

  11
 Our partnership with the World’s Largest Swimming Lesson continued as part of our
ongoing mission to emphasize that “swimming lessons save lives.” The event was free
to the public and co-hosted by the South Gate Aqua Coalition (SGAC), drawing nearly
200 attendees.

Free Community Swim Days also made a big splash this quarter. We hosted the
Summer Kick-Off Splash (June), 4th of July Splash, and Back-to-School
Splash (August). Each event welcomed approximately 100 attendees, offering a free
family swim session and family-friendly lawn games to promote water safety, recreation,
and community engagement.

Fitness
In the first quarter of this year, we experienced a positive trend in Sports Center
memberships. We sold or renewed a total of 4,000 memberships. The Fitness
membership segment was particularly strong, accounting for 66% of all memberships
sold. This growth indicates that majority are increasingly drawn to our fitness classes,
programs, and gym facilities.

Sports Center check-ins for the quarter reached approximately 21,000. Fitness
memberships continue to account for the majority of check-ins totaling around 14,500
(66%), while Sports Center Daily admissions came in at approximately 4,000. The bulk
of daily admissions were for Sports Adult with over 1500 drop-ins during the quarter.
With the presence of the Junior Athletic Association’s indoor basketball season during
this period there was less open gym availability, contributing to a decrease in drop-in
recreation basketball participants. We expanded our group exercise class schedule: two
HIIT classes, one Advanced Yoga, one Combo Boxing and one more Zumba class in
the mornings. All new classes were well received with attendance steadily increasing.
Currently, the Sports Center offers 38 group exercises classes per week!

Personal training services have remained relatively steady, with a total of 23 packages
sold last quarter to now a total of 22 packages sold this quarter. The 12-session private
package and the 16-session semi-private option continue to be the most sought-after
choices, despite this being a slower season for personal training as many of our clients
participate in the Biggest Loser Challenge.

We successfully hosted our 4th Annual Fun Run on Saturday, July 19, attracting over
550 registered runners and several hundred spectators. Each participant received a
complimentary T-shirt, and headband. The one-mile course featured a variety of fun
elements, including inflatable obstacle courses, water slides, a mud pit, ice crawl, foam
areas, and plenty of splash zones. This year the event was sponsored by Tampico and
Amazon.

Youth Sports:
The first quarter kicked off with strong participation, as all youth fundamental sports
classes filled within just a few hours of opening registration for the summer session. Our
core programs—basketball, volleyball, baseball, multi-sport, and soccer—remained
highly popular, offering introductory drills and lessons in each respective sport. For the
fall registration, class formats were slightly modified to incorporate new drills and
training methods aimed at enhancing player development.
  Page 2 of 7

  12
 Karate contract classes also saw high demand this summer. Instructor Juan Larios
continues to deliver high-quality instruction, teaching students both the techniques and
values of Karate. Additionally, Juan Larios’ dojo hosted its annual International Karate
Tournament on September 14, which featured competitors from Ecuador, Nicaragua, El
Salvador, and local athletes. The event was a success, drawing over 190 competitors
and 500 spectators.

Lastly, the Rec on the Run program wrapped up in August, providing engaging
recreational activities for the community during the Concerts in the Park series.

Adult Sports:
The first quarter of Adult Sports concluded on a high note, with new champions crowned
in both the Men’s and Co-ed Softball leagues. This season saw strong participation,
with 40 teams competing across seven divisions, each battling weekly for the top spot.
Champions were awarded redesigned championship hoodies along with team trophies.
Fall registration brought in another impressive turnout, with 38 teams spread across 6
divisions.

“Basketball After Dark” returned on July 2, featuring eight teams competing in pool-play
format followed by a single-elimination tournament. The winning team took home
custom shirts and backpacks. Building on that success, we introduced the first-ever
“Dodgeball After Dark” event on July 16. Five teams participated, with the champions
receiving a South Gate water bottle and branded sack-pack.

Open Play Volleyball on Tuesday nights remained a community favorite, drawing over
800 drop-in participants this quarter. Due to its popularity, we launched the inaugural
“Volleyball After Dark” event on July 29, which featured 8 teams. The winning team
received custom shirts and sack-packs.

The South Gate Sports Center Gymnasium recently underwent a significant scoreboard
upgrade. Planning began in early 2025 and was completed in September. The
improvements include new scoreboards for the main court, and smaller scoreboards for
the two auxiliary courts. In addition, shot clocks were installed on all courts—an
enhancement that sets the facility apart, as few recreation centers in the area offer this
feature.

Currently, we are in the recruitment phase for the upcoming Men’s and Women’s
Basketball Leagues, aiming to launch the season this winter.

Sports Partner Organizations:
The South Gate Aztecs began their Fall Season preparations with practices on
Diamonds 9 and 10 at South Gate Park every Tuesday and Wednesday.

SGJAA’s baseball and softball summer seasons ran smoothly, attracting hundreds of
youth who filled the park six days a week. Their highly popular summer Basketball
League also operated seamlessly throughout the season and culminated with a friendly
  Page 3 of 7

  13
 and competitive Coaches vs. Staff game where the JAA earned the hard-fought victory.

AYSO continues to be a major presence at Hollydale Regional Park, with over 30 teams
practicing and playing games daily across five lined fields. The Fall season remains
their busiest, with numerous teams filling the park throughout the week.

Youth Programs
The Tot Time and Tiny Two’s programs came to an end on the week of August 21. The
final day featured themed activities—Camping Day for Tiny Two’s and a Water Play
Area for Tot Time. Three new staff members were hired and shadowed classes during
this time. A television has been installed in Room B for Tiny Two’s use to expand
lessons and offer interactive components. Our Lil Chef program was again at full
capacity for both sessions. Many recipes were reviewed and executed, our final week
featured birthday cake soft-baked cookies and Monte Cristo sandwiches.

Special Events:
This year’s Summer Concerts in the Park series featured an incredible lineup of
performances, including Mariachi Divas, Knyght Ryder, Vilma Diaz y La Sonora, Those
Guys, and Los Del Momento. We moved all performances to Thursday evenings in July
and extended the event by an hour, running from 6pm to 9pm. The additional hour
allotted to each concert was to keep the party going as we added in a DJ dance party
spinning the hottest tunes for all to enjoy.

We also modified the event layout, relocating the beer garden closer to the stage to
enhance the concert experience. Each event showcased a delicious selection of food
trucks, including Lucille’s BBQ, Tijuanas Birria, Adamz Pizza Stop, Sending Noods,
Tacos al Cabron, Churro Panzon, Inglorious Funnels, and Kona Ice. Tap Truck LA
operated the beer garden, while Tampico distributed complimentary products to guests.
Inside the beer garden, attendees could relax and play a variety of board and card
games. Guests also enjoyed fun giveaways, such as color-changing cups, inflatable
instruments, koozies, beach balls, and glow sticks. Additionally, Rec on the Run
provided engaging children’s activities at every concert, ensuring fun for the whole
family.

Our 4th Annual Zine Fiesta took place on Saturday, July 26. We hosted 15

the event we celebrated with a pinata as it is a Zine Fiesta! On the museum side we

and tell them about how they created Zines, they felt our Zine Fiesta was less
transactional and more community building compared to other Zine events. That gives
us great joy to know that artists feel connected and valued by our communities.
